If the lake is part of your Sunday, take the wind advisory seriously: south winds run 20 to 30 knots this morning, with waves up to 3 feet. It’s already raining in Burlington, and the rain should ease after 11, but this is not a clean break. Several rounds of showers are possible through the afternoon, with a few thunderstorms mixed in, and the forecasters see a small chance, under 15 percent, of a stronger storm. The European model is wetter than the official forecast, so I’d bet on carrying the rain jacket. Keep plans flexible, and stay off the broad lake in those stronger south winds.

Tonight brings another chance for storms, especially after midnight, before a much sharper Monday. Monday looks mostly sunny with a high near 67, but northwest winds could still reach 25 knots on the lake. The best call is an indoor or close-to-home Sunday, then save the waterfront for Monday afternoon once the wind settles.

WCAX METEOROLOGIST (regional station — Burlington relevance only, never their branding): BURLINGTON, Vt. (WCAX) - A low pressure system to our south will bring showers tonight and into Sunday morning. There’s the chance for a thunderstorm. It will be breezy and much warmer tonight with lows in the upper 50s to low 60s. That low will move away from our region Sunday morning, with the rest of the day being mostly cloudy with widely scattered showers. During the afternoon and early evening, a few thunderstorms may form along a cold front. Even an isolated severe storm can’t be ruled out, but the risk is quite low. Highs on Sunday will be in the 70s, though western New Hampshire may be in the 60s due to the later departure of showers.
